messages:
alex: FYI support escalation from ACME — seeing p99 jumps on /v1/generate in prod-us-east-1 since ~06:00 UTC. p50 stable, p99 went from ~2s to ~8s. ticket SUP-9123. https://console.redwood/alerts/9123
support-bot: alert: p99_generate_latency prod-us-east-1 = 8.12s (+4.1s vs baseline), anomaly_score=6.2
maria: @alex curious — any recent continuous-batcher config rollouts? linger/hold changes often cause tail for tiny prompts
alex: rolled a batcher config at 06:10 (was on-call). changed max_batch_size 64->128 and hold_ms 4->12. rollout id: roll-2026-1749995500
alex: here's the diff we applied:
```diff
- max_batch_size: 64
- hold_ms: 4
+ max_batch_size: 128
+ hold_ms: 12
```
sam: that combo can increase p99 for low-QPS/small-response patterns. ACME traffic profile? lots of short prompts?
alex: yes — ACME traces show many short prompts (20-40 tokens) and bursty arrivals. p50 < 300ms, p95 ~600ms, p99 spiking to 7-8s.
jessica: quick mitigation proposal: rollback hold_ms to 6ms and pin max_batch_size=64 for prod-us-east-1 (or per-tenant override for ACME). I can hotpatch the canary.
maria: can we get repro script so we can test before/after? want to simulate ACME bursty tiny prompts.
sam: repro loadgen (10 concurrent clients, short prompts, 100ms inter-arrival):
```bash
# simple loadgen to reproduce tiny-prompt tail
for i in {1..10}; do
  (while true; do
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"prompt": "hello", "max_tokens": 32}' &
    sleep 0.1
  done) &
done
wait
```
alex: running repro against prod-canary now, reproduces p99 ~7.9s. captured a trace showing requests waiting in batcher for hold_ms window then long serialize time when batch large and many tiny responses.
jessica: ok pushing hotpatch: set hold_ms=6 and max_batch_size=64 for canary group (rg-10). will route 5% traffic first.
ops-bot: canary rollout initiated: roll-2026-1749995700 -> prod-us-east-1/rg-10 (5% traffic)
alex: monitoring metrics — within 3 minutes p99 on canary dropped to ~3.1s (from 7.9). p95 unaffected.
maria: good signal. what about KV cache and decoding overhead? any correlation?
sam: KV misses add a bit but main driver here is batching wait + heavy serialization when batch contains many short outputs. increasing hold_ms increased chance of building big batches that hurt the tail for short-response customers.
jessica: rolling to 50% now and opening rollback flag if p99 >= previous baseline for >5m.
ops-bot: rollout update: 50% -> success so far
alex: ACME support notified, they reported degraded UX but accept canary plan.
maria: follow-up work: implement adaptive hold_ms based on observed prompt token histogram and a tiny-request fastpath that flushes smaller batches earlier. filing infra task.
jessica: created INF-2334: "adaptive-batcher-fastpath — adaptive hold_time & per-tenant min_batch" and added priority P1 for next sprint.
sam: thumbs up. after full rollout p99 reduced to ~2.9s cluster-wide. closing escalation? :thumbsup:
support-bot: incident SUP-9123 status changed -> resolved (root cause: continuous-batcher config change incompatible with short-prompt workload); follow-up INF-2334 filed.
